The ACGME’s DEI mandates are textbook bureaucratic overreach—diverting focus from clinical excellence to ideological compliance. Taxpayers fund residency programs to train skilled physicians, not activists. The suspension of this policy is a win for patients and meritocracy.

When accreditors prioritize race-based quotas over competency, they undermine trust in medical education and jeopardize care quality. Bill Title exposed how similar mandates funneled millions into administrative bloat instead of addressing physician shortages or improving rural access.

Real reform means cutting red tape, not inserting politics into life-saving training. Let’s restore rigor—patients deserve doctors trained in science, not social engineering.
